Download your scorecards from the dAImond Inning app

Source: R/daimond_api.R
daimond_games.Rd

Fetch reviewed play-by-play and pitcher lines for the scorecards saved in your dAImond Inning account. The plays use the same columns as import_scorecards(), so they work directly with every analysis function in this package.

Usage

daimond_games(
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  league = NULL,
  base_url = getOption("daimondstats.base_url", "https://daimondinning.com")
)

Arguments

from, to

Optional first and last game dates as Date or "YYYY-MM-DD" text.

league

Optional league filter, such as "mlb" or a league name used in the app.

base_url

App address. Defaults to the daimondstats.base_url option, or https://daimondinning.com.

Value

A list with three data frames:

  • games: one row per scorecard with game_id, game_date, league, game_pk, home_team, away_team, and scored_side.

  • plays: the seven columns of import_scorecards() plus game_date, jersey, and lineup_slot. game_id is the app's scorecard id.

  • pitchers: game_id, game_date, team, pitcher, outs, bf, pitches, h, bb, so, and needs_review.

Details

Requires an API key (see daimond_auth()) and an internet connection. Results are paged by the server and combined here. Entries the app still marks for review keep needs_review = TRUE; the analysis functions refuse them until they are corrected in the app.

Errors are reported in plain language: a missing or revoked key, a plan without API access, too many requests, or the app being unreachable.

See also

daimond_auth(), calculate_youth_stats(), check_pitch_counts()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
daimond_auth("di_pat_your_key_here")
season <- daimond_games(from = "2026-04-01", to = "2026-07-31")
calculate_youth_stats(season$plays)
} # }
